label: Contract-priced sell and burn
summary: Compose standalone contract-defined price formation with automatic destruction of sold inventory without assuming a v4 pool, hook, AMM, or liquidity position.
requiredFacts: Exact purchase, sale, redemption and price-formation formulas with units, domain, rounding and every boundary
Which sold tokens are received, escrowed and irreversibly burned, and how total supply is reconstructed
Reserve, collateral or settlement assets, solvency assumptions and the user exit when price formation or funding fails
Whether any market is Programmable-canonical; a standalone external or non-launchable contract market has zero canonical fee scopes and no fabricated hook or fee-policy instance
Executed gross quote-side volume and the matching Fee V2 collection profile only for each separately declared Programmable-canonical scope
Every mutable parameter, emergency power and authority, including whether any actor can mint, seize, redirect, pause or change the curve
requiredFiles: Curve and deflation specification with worked examples
Token, contract-price, burn and settlement source
Supply, reserve, fee and custody reconstruction index
requiredTests: Buy, sell, redemption and burn conservation against the independent model
Monotonicity, exponential or other declared deflation behavior, rounding and uint256 boundaries
Aggregate-versus-fragmented execution, partial fills, microtrades and exact input/output behavior
Zero reserve, extreme price, exhausted inventory, cancellation, refund and failed-settlement behavior
No mint, burn, reserve, fee, authority or alternative-market bypass
Quote-to-execution parity and explicit provider incompatibility behavior
risks: A pricing or rounding error can create free value, over-burn supply or make redemptions insolvent
A privileged curve, mint, burn or reserve control can silently change the promised economics
Ordinary routers and quote providers may not simulate nonstandard execution correctly
